newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares cling to highs, eye further ascent.
newsitem.headline: German shares cling to highs, eye further ascent.

text.p: German shares were holding firmly ahead at record levels in afternoon dealings on Wednesday, with many dealers predicting more gains to come as liquidity conditions remain supportive.
"There is no reason today for prices to fall," said a Frankfurt dealer.
"The dollar is up, Bunds are good: as long as this environment remains positive, I can see a lot of records ahead," he added.
The IBIS DAX index was up 44.69 points, or 1.17 percent, at 3,805.21 points, above the psychologically key 3,800 level.

At the same time, dealers conceded that much of the ascent was due to window-dressing before the end of the second quarter, with many noting that many German funds appeared to be underinvested in the market.
"At the moment, this is a volume-driven market. As long as the liquidity is there, we should stand up to whatever Wall Street can throw at us," a Munich dealer said.
"But there are not a lot of fundamental stories about."
The winners of the day were banking shares, dragged up in the wake of Deutsche Bank AG which surged after breaching a key resistance levl of 100 marks on Tuesday.
Deutsche was up 2.10 marks at 103.95 marks in afternoon trade.
Chemical shares were also in vogue after coming under some pressure recently after negative analysts' comments.
BASF AG was trading up 1.30 marks at 64.15 marks amid solid volumes in afternoon trade.
